name: Merck stitch otoplasty

lead: The Merck stitch is a closed ear-pinning technique placing sutures through small puncture incisions instead of an open posterior incision. It was published in 2013.

paras: Sutures placed through stab incisions reshape the cartilage without cutting it.
General suture-otoplasty risks include suture extrusion, hematoma, infection and recurrence; no technique-specific studies were found.

lead: The Merck stitch is a closed, minimally invasive otoplasty method in which sutures are placed through small stab incisions to reshape the ear without cutting the cartilage. Wikipedia dates its publication to 2013.[1]

It falls within the suture-only (cartilage-intact) group of otoplasty techniques and is contrasted with Mustardé's open approach, which uses a larger incision.[1] Published sources reviewed here give limited detail, and no clinical studies were found.

paras: Wikipedia describes the Merck method as closed and minimally invasive, using small stab incisions and leaving the cartilage intact, in contrast to Mustardé's open approach with mattress sutures and skin excision.[1] The broader literature on otoplasty complications lists suture extrusion as the most common problem with suture-based approaches.[1]

timeline.event: Merck publishes the closed stitch method.[1]
